items.claim: The unit correctly reads Isa.9.1-Isa.9.7 as one syntactically continuous declaration and discloses the zone-A hazard stack (throne names, the exegesis note, the ketiv/qere doubled token) as corroboration rather than as an undisclosed driver.
items.evidence: The chain of ki-clauses from web:Isa.9.3 through web:Isa.9.7 carries one uninterrupted argument with no fresh subject reopening before web:Isa.9.8 = oshb:Isa.9.7's dabar-shalach clause; the setumah mark at oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7) is disclosed as tier-3 single-witness corroboration for a close already argued from the ki-chain, the OSHB exegesis note at the same verse is named as apparatus rather than text bytes, and the ketiv/qere note at oshb:Isa.9.2 (= web:Isa.9.3) is checked and disclosed without a content claim resting on either reading. All zone-A refs carry the required duals.

items.claim: The unit is well-bounded at the fresh word-sent subject-change and the first stretched-hand refrain occurrence, with correct zone-A duals and honest disclosure of the 5:25-bridge single-poem rival.
items.evidence: web:Isa.9.8 = oshb:Isa.9.7 opens with a new grammatical subject (the sent word) replacing the throne-clause's referent, and the unit closes at the byte-identical refrain בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.11 = web:Isa.9.12, byte tier); the setumah mark at oshb:Isa.9.6 is disclosed as front-seam corroboration only, and the row names the live rival that folds this stanza into one continuous poem from web:Isa.5.25 (sweep: 5 verses) without adopting it.
tier_citations: marks inventory: SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.9.6 and oshb:Isa.9.11

items.claim: Confidence sits at high for a stanza-cut inside the 9:7-10:4 refrain poem, a hazard zone the strategy holds should not sit unexamined at high, and the jump above the immediately preceding stanza's medium rating is not supported by any stanza-specific evidence.
items.evidence: The row's own strongest_rejected_alternative discloses the identical live rival (a single continuous poem opening at web:Isa.5.25, sweep: 5 verses) that the immediately preceding stanza (web:Isa.9.8-web:Isa.9.12) carries at medium confidence; both stanzas rest on the same byte-identical refrain bracket בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.11 and oshb:Isa.9.16, byte tier) and the same rival architecture, so nothing in this stanza's own bytes supports rating it above its neighbor.

items.claim: Confidence sits at high for another stanza-cut inside the same 9:7-10:4 refrain poem, again without a stanza-specific reason for rating above the run's opening stanza, contrary to the strategy's own hazard-zone caution.
items.evidence: The refrain bracket at oshb:Isa.9.20 (= web:Isa.9.21, byte tier) closes this stanza on the identical bytes בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה as the other three, and the disclosed 5:25-bridge rival (sweep: 5 verses) carries the same structural uncertainty as the run's first stanza, which is rated medium; the forecast list names the 9:7-10:4 stanza cuts as a zone that should not sit at unexamined high.

items.claim: The unit correctly identifies its own dual character - a woe-onset opening bound to the surrounding refrain-poem's closing bracket - and discloses both the mark layer and the 5:25-bridge rival honestly rather than folding one into the other.
items.evidence: The hoy-onset opens the unit at oshb:Isa.10.1 (byte tier) while the unit still closes on the same refrain bytes בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה at oshb:Isa.10.4 = web:Isa.10.4; device_notes names the dual woe/refrain-stanza character explicitly instead of defaulting silently to one reading, and the setumah marks at oshb:Isa.9.20 (= web:Isa.9.21) and oshb:Isa.10.4 are both correctly typed against the inventory.
tier_citations: marks inventory: SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.9.20 and oshb:Isa.10.4

items.claim: The addressee shift from decree-writers to Assyria at the hoy-onset, and the closing rhetorical question before the next unit's response formula, are well-argued tier-1 seams with correctly typed mark disclosure.
items.evidence: The Assyria hoy-onset opens at oshb:Isa.10.5 (byte tier) against a wholly different addressee than the preceding unit's decree-writers, and the unit closes at the Jerusalem/Samaria rhetorical question (web:Isa.10.11) before the next unit's temporal-response formula opens; the setumah marks at oshb:Isa.10.4 and oshb:Isa.10.11 are both correctly typed SAMEKH, matching the inventory.
tier_citations: marks inventory: SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.10.4 and oshb:Isa.10.11

items.claim: The response-formula onset at web:Isa.10.12 and the internal therefore-clause at web:Isa.10.16 are correctly read as one continuing divine reply rather than a fresh seam, and the row correctly discloses both bounding parashah marks under their own distinct types.
items.evidence: The response-formula opens the divine reply at oshb:Isa.10.12 (byte tier) with no addressee change at the internal therefore-clause of oshb:Isa.10.16; the setumah mark at oshb:Isa.10.11 and the petuchah mark at oshb:Isa.10.19 are both correctly typed against the inventory, and the row correctly distinguishes the plain remnant noun in the forest image at oshb:Isa.10.19 from the name-reactivating material that follows.
tier_citations: marks inventory: SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.10.11, PE at oshb:Isa.10.19

items.claim: device_notes misassigns web:Isa.10.22 to the plain-common-noun remnant object when its own letter bytes carry the identical two-word collocation that constitutes the name-reactivating clause at web:Isa.10.21, so the remnant-object disclosure blends two distinct objects instead of naming the object first.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.10.21 opens with שְׁאָ֥ר יָשׁ֖וּב (byte tier) and oshb:Isa.10.22 carries the identical contiguous pair שְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב (byte tier) - the same collocation that names the son's sign at oshb:Isa.7.3 (וּשְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב, vav-prefixed); this is distinct from oshb:Isa.10.20's bare שְׁאָ֤ר construct (she'ar Yisrael), which carries no adjacent yashuv verb at all. device_notes nonetheless groups web:Isa.10.22 with web:Isa.10.20 as the plain common noun, contrary to this object grouping.
tier_citations: byte tier: oshb:Isa.10.20, oshb:Isa.10.21, oshb:Isa.10.22, oshb:Isa.7.3
